newsitem.title: USA: U.S. jobless claims unch latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. jobless claims unch latest week.

text.p: U.S. Labor Department report of initial state jobless benefit claims, seasonally adjusted.
Week Ended Initial Claims 4-Week Avg. Continued Claims
R-Revised, Nov 16 Initial Claims from 344,000 and Nov 9 from 327,000; Nov 9 4-Week Average from 330,000; Nov 9 Continued Claims from 2,499,000 and Nov 2 from 2,480,000.
Wall Street economists had forecast jobless claims filings of 336,000 in the November 23 week.
The department said three states reported increases in initial claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended November 16, the latest period for which the data are available.

They were Illinois, with 1,800; Ohio, with 1,762; and New Jersey with 1,520. Illinois and New Jersey reported layoffs in the trade and service industries. Illinois also had layoffs in manufacturing. Ohio said there were seasonal layoffs in various industries across the state.
There were seven states reporting decreases in initial claims exceeding 1,000, unadjusted, in the November 16 week.
They were California, with 8,067; Texas, with 3,189; Louisiana, with 1,666; Washington, with 1,489; Michigan, with 1,308; Oregon, with 1,301; and Florida, with 1,261.

California cited fewer layoffs in the service industry and agriculture and Michigan reported fewer layoffs in the auto industry. Florida said there were fewer layoffs in construction, trade and service industries, manufacturing and agriculture.
Texas, Louisiana, Washington and Oregon gave no explanation for their decreases.
